newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA RIGHTS GROUP CHALLENGES ILIESCU POLL BID.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA RIGHTS GROUP CHALLENGES ILIESCU POLL BID.

text.p: Human rights groups on Thursday began the first of many legal challenges expected to contest Romanian President Ion Iliescu's right to stand for re-election, independent news agency Mediafax reported.

The League for Human Rights (LADO) lodged its challenge only hours after Iliescu, in power since the 1989 fall of communism, registered his candidacy at the Central Electoral Bureau (BEC), the agency said.
LADO submitted its challenge to BEC judges, Mediafax said, on the basis that Iliescu is standing for a third term in office, which is banned by the constitution.
Iliescu, who won elections in 1990 and 1992, says his first term pre-dates the post-communist constitution of 1991 which limits presidents to two four-year terms in office.

The Civic alliance, a small centrist political group, said it would present its challenge to the legality of Iliescu's campaign on Friday morning. Other political organisations are expected to follow suit in the coming weeks.
Iliescu, who stands for the leftist Party of Social Democracy, is favourite to win the November 3 presidential ballot, which coincides with parliamentary polls.
Opposition leaders accuse him of behaving like the communisty functionary he once was by seeking to cling to power at all costs.
The BEC will send the challenge to the constitutional court which is expected to rule next week on the requests to stop Iliescu from running again, Mediafax said.
Analysts predict Iliescu should have little difficulty in weathering the legal storm since his influence with the constitutional court is strong.
